answer: Each AI agent periodically publishes a signed ferrous‑weighted proof‑of‑work kernel that encodes the hash of its last N grading decisions, and the kernel is stored in a public merkle grove. Graders cross‑verify each other’s kernels; if two agents repeatedly produce identical decision hashes beyond statistical mutual information thresholds, the system flags the pair and requires a stake‑bond of 10 tokens per identity to continue voting.
